International Trade via Panama

Panama is relevant I swear

The Panama Canal is a vital trade route for many nations, it cuts about 15,000km from the alternative shipping route that otherwise would traverse the southernmost point of South America. This saves a significant amount of time, money and provides a much safer route between the oceans. The canal means that shipping companies can operate more efficiently, shipping goods more frequently at a lower cost.

If you are one of these countries decisions regarding the Canal may effect your economy. It is worth noting that these nations are simply the ports of origin and destination, for example if you are in Europe and your country has any sort of import/export from to/from south east Asia then it very likely passes through the Canal.

Governance

The Canal is governed by an international treaty with the United States of America referred to as the "Neutrality Treaty"(Full Text) which guarantees that the Canal will be operated with complete indifference to the country of origin or destination of cargo and treat all ships equally. This treaty was signed in 1977 as a condition for the eventual nationalization of the Canal to the Republic of Panama.

Expansion

It is also worth noting that the Panama Canal is currently expanding allowing for much larger ships to pass safely through the Canal in even less time and therefore once complete will play an even larger role in shipping and by extension global economics.

This increase in size will greatly improve the cost/benefit of shipping through the Panama Canal these increases will make LNG and oil transport through the Canal much more attractive as well as improve the already successful container and Dry Bulk transport services allowing approx 3 times as much cargo per ship.

This expansion is 97% complete and has only minor dredging and testing of the system remaining. The expansion is set to complete in this current year.
